messages:
samir: Quick sync — we need to reconcile headroom signals across dedicated pools. Predictive prewarm works for steady diurnal patterns but customers still hit cold tails during bursty windows. Thoughts?
clare: Agree. Main problem seems to be mismatched signal sources: tenant forecast vs operator pool telemetry. They drift and autoscaler double-counts.
jon: +1. Also the burst lane admission currently assumes infinite warm capacity which is false with MIG fragmentation. We've seen 503s.
esra: Can we separate admission into a fastpath (burst credits) and a slowpath (predictive warmup)? So the fastpath admits only if credit and a local KV cache hit.
samir: That matches what I sketched. Proposal: hybrid mode with conservative predictive prewarm (uses workload-level forecasts) + small burst lane with tokenized credits per tenant. If credits exhausted, fallback to queued admission with an SLA-derived wait time.
clare: How do we allocate credits? static per-SLA or dynamic based on recent usage? Dynamic could be gamed by noisy tenants.
jon: We should combine both: a baseline grant per subscription tier + ephemeral credits earned by steady usage. Baseline prevents starvation, earned credits avoid penalizing well-behaved tenants.
esra: What about operator boundary? Should the pool orchestrator manage credits or the higher-level controller? My vote: keep credit accounting in the control plane (operator) for global fairness and in-pool admission agent only consults a compact lease token.
samir: Agreed — operator owns global accounting. Admission agent gets signed lease tokens like: 
```json
{"tenant":"acme","credits":3,"exp":1718504600,"sig":"..."}
```
agent verifies signature, decrements locally on admission. That keeps per-request latency low.
clare: Nice. We need TTLs to avoid stale credits being used after scale down. Make exp conservative.
jon: Also implement a credit-replenish hook: when pool goes from cold->warm and affirms availability, operator tops up ephemeral credits to recent active tenants.
esra: Edge-case: what if predictive prewarm accidentally pins GPUs for low-value tenants? Need cost guardrails. Maybe a scoring function: score = value*latency_sensitivity / cost_estimate and only prewarm above threshold.
samir: I like the scoring idea. Let's add a simple config prototype: 
```yaml
autoscaler:
  mode: hybrid
  predictive:
    enabled: true
    window_seconds: 600
    lookahead_seconds: 120
    score_threshold: 0.6
  burst_lane:
    enabled: true
    baseline_credits_by_tier:
      free: 1
      standard: 3
      enterprise: 10
    ephemeral_multiplier: 0.2
    token_ttl_seconds: 3600
```
clare: Where do we record billing/cost impact? Need token-level traces in Console + cost delta estimates for each prewarm decision.
jon: We should also expose a dry-run mode in the operator so customers can preview prewarm decisions for a given traffic trace.
esra: Ops note: implement circuit-breaker when pool fragmentation > 30% or MIG unallocatable fraction > 0.15, disable burst lane and route to compatible model variants.
samir: Good. Action items: 1) Esra to draft operator token format & verification flow. 2) Clare to run sim on historical tenant traces and tune score_threshold. 3) Jon to prototype local admission agent with signed token check. 4) I'll add observability hooks for token-level accounting and cost delta.
clare: +1, I'll add a small spreadsheet with simulation assumptions.
jon: I'll start a branch for admission-agent shim, will post a tiny demo log: 
[admit] tenant=acme credits=2 token_ok=true admitted=true latency=23ms
orch-bot: deploy:autoscaler v2 queued for staging. PR #4821
samir: Perfect — sync tomorrow 10am to review sims.
